Subject: Finly discovery recap — p95 latency & streaming concurrency

Hi Samir & Priya,

Thanks again for taking the time today — appreciate the context on Finly's in-product assistant. Quick recap from our side to make sure we're aligned on the immediate pain, goals, and next steps.

Pain points we heard
- Interactive UX is hurting: p95 generation latency for the assistant is currently ~1.2s (measured on peak traffic), which leads to visible lag for users.
- Streaming experience inconsistent: first-token latency and steady token cadence vary between regions, causing choppy streaming in the UI.
- Concurrency/throughput gaps: you expect ~500 concurrent live users for the new feature with bursts up to ~2k during peak jobs. Current infra spikes lead to queueing and timeouts.

Current stack (high level)
- Primary model calls go to a managed LLM endpoint on GCP (NVIDIA A100-backed instances).
- Local prefix caching for common prompts; however cache hit rate is low for personalized queries.
- In-house routing + a small GPU pool for latency-sensitive requests.

Success criteria we discussed
- P95 generation latency <= 300ms for 90% of traffic (target 250ms for key flows).
- Streaming UX: first token < 200ms, steady token cadence for subsequent tokens so the UI appears smooth.
- Support sustained 500 concurrent active users with graceful scaling to 2k bursts without >500ms added queuing latency.
- Clear telemetry showing tail improvements and regression alerts.

Proposed next steps
1) Tech deep-dive: schedule a 60–90 minute session with your infra/SRE and our SE (Aditya) to map current telemetry and identify quick wins (autoscaling, batching, caching).
2) Share artifacts: we've attached a draft architecture diagram and our SLA matrix for reference. Please share any current load tests or telemetry dashboards you have (Prometheus/Grafana links).
3) PoC proposal: we'll put together a short PoC plan (4–6 weeks) that focuses on streaming-first optimizations and p95 tail reduction.

If that looks right, we can lock the deep-dive for next week. Aditya — can you do Wed/Thu next week?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. Confirming the notes and adding a couple of specifics from our side: 

- Confirmed targets: p95 <= 300ms is our primary goal. For our analytics dashboard flows we can tolerate slightly higher but the customer-facing assistant must meet the 250–300ms range.
- Current measurements: our in-prod synthetic shows median ~180ms but p95 ~1.2s during peak; traces point to batching + long setup on the managed endpoint as main contributors.
- Privacy constraint: Certain requests must stay within our VPC (PII) — we'll highlight those in the deep-dive so we can discuss Private deployment options or IP allowlists.

PoC ask: can you include an estimate for both (a) hosted optimization (short-term) and (b) dedicated/private deployment (longer-term)? We'd like a cost + timeline view.

We're good to schedule the technical session next Wed or Thu afternoon (PDT). Priya, Samir, and Alex (infra) will join.

Hi Samir & team — thanks for the notes, happy to run the deep-dive. A few quick clarifications so I can prepare the right demos/tests: 

1) Baseline telemetry we'd need from you before the call:
   - End-to-end traces (request start -> first token -> last token) sampled at p50/p95/p99 with timestamps
   - Request size distribution (avg tokens, 90th/99th)
   - Concurrent active user estimate and burst profile (rps or concurrent sessions over 1-min windows)

2) For the PoC: we recommend two parallel tracks:
   - Host optimizations (2–4 week quick wins): kernel selection, improved batching heuristics, streaming-first routing to reduce first-token latency.
   - Dedicated/Private pilot (4–8 week): reserved capacity + network placement to remove setup overhead and host PII flows.

3) Quick demo checklist (I'll prepare):
   - Live streaming demo highlighting first-token time and token cadence improvement
   - Simulated load showing p95 improvements at target concurrency ranges
   - Cost delta estimates for hosted vs dedicated

I can join Wed/Thu afternoon PDT next week — Marissa, please pick a slot and I'll block it.

Thanks,
